title: Construct a common complex product chart for the actual centre0 pair
body:
## Summary

Construct a common complex product chart for the actual PR5101 centre0 pair, answering the complex-chart question left open by JoyboyBrian's [PR5130](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5130). Claim type: scoped written algebraic construction with exact finite corroboration. This result was produced by Nick Petalas.

```text
A = G direct-sum I, B = G^T direct-sum I
S = inverse negacyclic evaluation * inverse common weighted-swap basis
(S A S^-1 x)(S B S^-1 z) = (S B S^-1)(xz)
```

The identity holds for every x,z in C[y]/(y^N+1) and every N>=112, including all claimed power-of-two paddings N>=128. Seven active planes have product eigenvalues 937 +/- 12 sqrt(6097); their shared weighted-swap basis and the fixed complement give an explicit S over Q(sqrt(6097), zeta_(2N)). The invertible output map is S B S^-1 itself. The same construction supplies the slightly broader all-integer-N statement without an additional search.

Credit JoyboyBrian for the question and common Gaussian-rational obstruction; Chris R / Clear1nsight's [PR5101](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/5101) for the actual centre0 code; the Dugongue/mdumitrean PR4948/4929 lineage, Cao Yifan/intqwq, Cinna Davis and the retained native, analytic, precision and compiler contributors. Product isotopy, two-involution reduction and polynomial evaluation are classical. The predecessor results are cited premises, not audit deliverables. Their source files and credit lines are unchanged.

[Advance CLAIM](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/1166#discussioncomment-19377694).

## Evidence

Before, the common-Q(i) chart was excluded and the complex case was explicitly open. After, the written proof and exact constructor give a common complex chart and its inverse.

At head `528e9129f181b79ec044fa23fddb378a646305c8`:

- Exact quadratic arithmetic checks both inverse orders on 224 basis columns and both source endpoints on 224 columns, plus all 12,544 split basis products and 2,401 quadratic products.
- Eighteen literal negacyclic vector-pair tests at N=128,256,512 corroborate evaluation, normalization, padding and wrap signs over explicitly checked finite prime fields. Eleven controls exercise invalid boundaries, an altered inverse, a false common diagonal model, weights, wrap and an incorrect identity output map.
- Normal and optimized warning-strict direct runs print `PASS_CENTRE0_COMPLEX_PRODUCT_CHART`, timed locally at 3.87 and 3.89 seconds. The complete registered launcher passes both commands and prints `PASS_REGISTERED_RESEARCH_PACKAGE` in 10.32 seconds total. Each registered timeout is 180 seconds.
- Committed-byte/source-history preflight passes on all eleven publication/input files. The official eleven-file export passes integrity and declared-input coverage. Its read-only Git-free normal/optimized replays pass with unchanged bytes and modes. The generated receipt binds all seven other package files.

From the repository root, using the exact local CPython 3.12.15 interpreter, standard library only:

```sh
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -W error -B research/centre0-complex-product-chart/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -I -O -W error -B research/centre0-complex-product-chart/verify.py
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/research_package.py --package research/centre0-complex-product-chart
/Users/nick/git/integer-mult-bounds/.venv/bin/python3.12 -B scripts/check_research_commit.py --package research/centre0-complex-product-chart --check-source-history
```

A portable CPython 3.12 path can replace the local path. The local environment is macOS 27.0.1 arm64. The quantified complex theorem rests on the written proof; finite-field tests alone do not prove it.

## Limitations

This supplies an algebraic common chart. It does not commute the native K_i normalizers, emit a changed producer, implement the chart with rounded/native operations, establish independent Gaussian target eligibility, or price a complete paid/target invoice. Arbitrary dirty-helper restoration, ownership, precision/tape/storage/stock, compiler and outer admission remain separate. All five selected framework assumptions retain their status. No new kappa, supplier admission, selected-frontier change, complete multiplication theorem or runtime improvement is claimed. No selected cold replay, historical full replay, Lean or Docker run was performed. Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

## Open next questions

- Implement S and its inverse at one actual normalized native caller, charging preparation, conversion, delivery and restoration before testing the complete signed bill. A physical chart implementation is missing.
- For that implementation, bound both chart norms and every arithmetic prefix to obtain a paid precision/storage contract. Invertibility alone gives no affordable finite-grid prescription.

## Related open work

Completion refresh listed all 204 account open PRs and inspected the twelve other open contributions created since the advance CLAIM. None studies this actual centre0 common-product-chart identity or reports a conflicting shared quantity. No extra computation was run to check those contributions.

No open PR studying this actual centre0 common-product-chart identity was found in the final live object search. Merged PR5130 and PR5101 supply the source and question. The active coded-caller investigation in [Discussion4930](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/4930) concerns physical native/caller closure; this algebraic construction does not deliver that closure.
